# CompositorManager

> **File:** `services/CompositorManager.qml` · **Docs:** see [docs/dev](../../README.md)

The running compositor, for the rest of axiom: its windows, outputs and workspaces in shapes that don't depend on it, what it supports, and every workspace switch and window focus (docs/dev/compositor/README.md). The compositor's own work is its backend's (HyprlandManager); with none (an unknown compositor) everything here is empty and does nothing.

### Properties

- `kind` (readonly string): Which compositor axiom runs under: "hyprland", "sway", "niri" or "" (unknown, or none).
- `backend` (readonly var): The backend for `kind`, or null (docs/dev/compositor/contract.md).
- `supports` (readonly var): What the compositor can do, by capability (contract.md › Capabilities): false for anything the backend doesn't say, and for what AXIOM_COMPOSITOR_OFF ("focusGrab,layerOrder") turns off, so the fallba…
- `windows` (readonly var): Every mapped window: [{ id, appId, initialAppId, title, workspaceId, workspaceName, output, floating, fullscreen, maximized, hidden, focusRank, x, y, w, h }]
- `outputs` (readonly var): Every monitor: [{ name, description, x, y, width, height, scale, focused, activeWorkspaceId, specialWorkspaceId, reserved }]
- `workspaces` (readonly var): Every workspace: [{ id, name, output, windowCount, active, focused }]
- `focusedOutput` (readonly string): The focused monitor's name, or "" with none
- `activeWindowId` (readonly string): The focused window's id, or ""
- `gapsOut` (readonly var): The gaps the compositor leaves at the screen edges, after reserved zones ({ top, right, bottom, left })
- `blur` (readonly var): The compositor's blur as in effect ({ enabled, size, passes })
- `splitWidthMultiplier` (readonly real): A tiled box wider than tall times this splits side by side
- `surfacesReady` (readonly bool): Whether surfaces with a fixed stacking order (bars, border, docks, edge menus, the desktop) may map yet: the backend's stacking is in
- `focused` (readonly var): The focused output, or null

### Signals

- `layersChanged()`: A layer surface opened or closed
- `outputsHotplugged()`: A monitor was added or removed
- `configReloaded()`: The compositor reloaded its config
- `keyboardLayoutChanged()`: The keyboard layout switched
- `windowFocused(string appId)`: A window was focused; appId is its app id (class)
- `workspaceWrapped(string output, bool alongRow, bool forward)`: A step about to wrap round the grid's ends on `output` (its name): along a row (`alongRow`, the standard layout's only kind) or a column, `forward` past the last.

### Functions

- `outputFor(screen)`: The output showing a screen, or null
- `output(name)`: The output named `name`, or null
- `activeWorkspaceId()`: The focused output's active workspace id (1 while unknown)
- `refresh()`: Re-reads the outputs and windows soon
- `focusWindow(id)`: Focuses a window.
- `closeWindow(id)`
- `placeWindow(id, workspaceId, targetId, side, restore, reinsert, floatAt)`: The overview's drag and drop (HyprlandManager.placeWindow)
- `resizeWindow(id, dw, dh, dx, dy)`: The overview's resize (HyprlandManager.resizeWindow)
- `toplevelFor(id)`: The live Wayland toplevel of a window (for previews), or null
- `hasFullscreen(name)`: Whether the named output's active workspace, or the special workspace open on it, shows a fullscreen window (maximized ones don't count: they leave reserved space alone)
- `biggestWindowForWorkspace(workspaceId)`: The largest window on a workspace (its icon stands for the workspace), or null
- `stripWindows(workspaceId, vertical)`: A workspace's windows in strip order (WorkspaceGeometry.stripOrder)
- `lastFocused(windows)`: Of `windows`, the one focused last (focused now, if any is), or null
- `withKeyboard(callback)`: Calls back with the main keyboard's layouts ({ layouts, index, keymap }), or null
- `cycleKeyboardLayout(direction, callback)`: Switches every keyboard to its "next" or "prev" layout, then calls back
- `withLayerRects(callback)`: Calls back with each output's layer surfaces ({ [output]: { w, h, layers: [{ namespace, x, y, w, h }] } }), or null when unknown
- `withCursorPos(callback)`: Calls back with the cursor's global position ({ x, y }), or null when the compositor can't say
- `withHoveredScreen(callback)`: Calls back with the name of the screen under the cursor (the focused one if the compositor can't say)
- `warpCursorToLayer(namespace, output, width, height, x, y)`: Moves the cursor to (x, y) inside one of axiom's layer surfaces (the one in `namespace` on `output`, `width` × `height`), where the compositor can
- `exitSession()`: Ends the session (the power menu's log out)
- `dpmsCommand(on)`: The shell command turning the screens off or on (the idle daemon's), or "" where axiom doesn't know one
- `goToWorkspace(id, mode, output, focusId)`: Goes to workspace `id`. mode: "go" (default), "move" (taking the focused window along) or "moveSilent" (sending it there, staying put).
- `stepWorkspace(direction, mode)`: One step left/right/up/down from the current workspace: within the output's grid, or through 1..count in the standard layout (where up is previous and down next).
- `nthWorkspace(n, mode)`: The n-th workspace (1-based) of the current row in a grid or perMonitor layout, or workspace n in the standard layout (number keybinds)
- `stepStrip(direction, output)`: Scrolls the strip of an output's active workspace a column on (1) or back (-1).
- `workspaceBase(output)`: First workspace id an output (its name) shows: 1 in the standard layout, else its block's (grid/perMonitor, one block per output in a stable order — the primary first, then the rest by a description-…
- `workspaceIds(output)`: The workspace ids an output (its name) shows, in order
